subject: MAX function
notes: VERDICT UPHELD after an independent attack on each of the format's three obligations. `FUNCTION MAX ( { argument-1 } … )`: both words underlined (required), parentheses required, braces-plus-ellipsis = one or more with no upper bound. (1) REQUIRED WORDS AND PARENTHESES - the grammar deliberately parses the parenthesized list as a SUPERSET, `functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? refModPart*` (read at source, both symbols exist), and the omission is caught at bind with a COBOL diagnostic rather than a parse error, which is a conforming rejection either way. (2) THE ELLIPSIS IS GENUINELY UNBOUNDED - the original record asserted 'Variadic, 1, inf' from the row; re-derived at source, the row is `Add(new("MAX", IntrinsicType.Numeric, IntrinsicArity.Variadic, 1, inf, "p", "MaxScaled", ...))` and `const int inf = int.MaxValue;` (IntrinsicCatalog.cs), so no hidden ceiling truncates the ellipsis. (3) THE ARGUMENT SEPARATOR - `functionArgList : functionArgument (FNARG_SEPARATOR? functionArgument)*` admits the §8.3.5 comma separator and bare juxtaposition alike. No optional phrase words exist in this format, so there is no unverified half. NOTE ON SCOPE: the FUNCTION-keyword-omitted form is §8.4.3.2's grant, not this format's - §15.59.2 underlines FUNCTION as required - so it is out of scope here and is not what this CONFORMS rests on. EDITION WINDOW as in AR-15.59.3-1, from Annex E only. EVIDENCE: PROBED, --std 2023.
